samasa.vigraha: चितः कला चित्कला; अथवा चित् एव कला चित्कला
samasa.vigraha_iast: citaḥ kalā citkalā; athavā cit eva kalā citkalā
samasa.explanation: kalā 'digit, part, subtle power' is the head. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'a digit of consciousness'; as a karmadhāraya: 'the subtle power that is consciousness'. t and k meet with no change.

components.meaning: digit (of the moon), a small part; subtle power

names.meaning: She who is the digit (kalā) of consciousness
names.significance: Traditionally the name is read as consciousness present in each being as a ray or digit of the infinite, as the moon's digits are parts of the one moon.

meaning_check.note: 'the consciousness in brahman' did not render kalā; the name is the kalā, digit or subtle power, of consciousness.

names.uncertain: ṣaṣṭhī ('a digit of consciousness') and karmadhāraya ('consciousness as subtle power') readings are both possible.

samasa.vigraha: आनन्दस्य कलिका आनन्दकलिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: ānandasya kalikā ānandakalikā
samasa.explanation: kalikā 'bud' is the head; ānanda 'bliss' stands to it in the genitive: 'the bud of bliss'.

names.meaning: She who is the bud of bliss
names.significance: As a bud holds the whole flower unopened, She holds bliss that blossoms in the devotee's heart.

samasa.vigraha: प्रेम रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रेमरूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: prema rūpam yasyāḥ sā premarūpā
samasa.explanation: rūpa 'form' is identified with preman 'love', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is love'. preman loses its n in the compound (prema-), a morphological change.

components.note: appears as prema- in the compound
rūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose form is love
names.significance: Love is not something She has but what She is; pure devotion (prema) toward Her is Her own form reflected in the devotee.

meaning_check.note: 'pure' was added; the name says love is Her form.

sandhi.rule: the m (an augment, as in vaśaṅkara, name 697) becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ) and then ṅ, the nasal of k's class (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: प्रियम् करोति इति प्रियङ्करी
samasa.vigraha_iast: priyam karoti iti priyaṅkarī
samasa.explanation: -kara 'making, doing' from √kṛ (suffix khac, which brings the augment m after the first member) is the head, with the feminine -ī; priya 'what is dear' is its object.

names.meaning: She who grants what is dear to Her devotees
names.significance: She does what is dear to those who love Her — granting their wishes and, above all, the dearest thing, Herself.
names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; priyaṅkarī is priya + karī, with the augment m (written ṅ before k).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound pārāyaṇa; the n of ayana becomes retroflex ṇ after the r of pāra (ṇatva)

samasa.vigraha: नाम्नाम् पारायणम् नामपारायणम्; नामपारायणेन प्रीता नामपारायणप्रीता
samasa.vigraha_iast: nāmnām pārāyaṇam nāmapārāyaṇam; nāmapārāyaṇena prītā nāmapārāyaṇaprītā
samasa.explanation: (1) nāma-pārāyaṇa 'the full recitation of the names' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; nāman loses its n). (2) The participle prītā 'pleased' is the head and takes that recitation in the instrumental of cause.

components.note: appears as nāma- in the compound
pāra 'the far shore' + ayana 'going': going through to the end

names.meaning: She who is pleased by the recitation of Her names
names.significance: Recitation of this Thousand Names is itself such a pārāyaṇa; the hymn's closing section (phalaśruti) praises its daily recitation.

meaning_check.note: pārāyaṇa is complete recitation, reading through to the end, rather than 'repetition'.

samasa.vigraha: नन्दिनः विद्या नन्दिविद्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: nandinaḥ vidyā nandividyā
samasa.explanation: vidyā 'mantra, sacred knowledge' is the head; Nandin (Nandi) stands to it in the genitive: 'the vidyā of Nandi'. nandin loses its n in the compound.

components.note: appears as nandi- in the compound

components.meaning: knowledge; in Śrīvidyā, a mantra of the Goddess

names.meaning: She who is the Vidyā (mantra) of Nandi
names.significance: Traditionally the Śrīvidyā mantra has forms associated with its great worshippers; Nandividyā is the form handed down through Nandikeśvara, and She is that mantra.

meaning_check.note: The name says She is the vidyā (mantra) of Nandi; 'worshipped by the Nandi mantra' reversed the relation.

names.previous_split_issues: Nandi's stem is nandin; vidyā here is a mantra, not general 'knowledge'.
names.uncertain: Which form of the mantra is meant by Nandividyā, and its place among the worshippers' vidyās, could not be confirmed against a printed commentary.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, with the feminine of relationship
samasa.vigraha: नटानाम् ईश्वरः नटेश्वरः; नटेश्वरस्य पत्नी नटेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: naṭānām īśvaraḥ naṭeśvaraḥ; naṭeśvarasya patnī naṭeśvarī
samasa.explanation: (1) naṭa-īśvara 'the lord of dancers', Śiva as Naṭarāja (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The feminine -ī denotes His wife (Pāṇini 4.1.48 puṃyogād ākhyāyām): 'the consort of the Lord of dancers'. Read directly as naṭānām īśvarī, it is 'the queen of dancers'.

names.meaning: She who is the consort of Naṭeśvara (Śiva, Lord of the dance)
names.significance: As Śiva dances the cosmic dance, She is His partner and witness; Her dance is the lāsya of name 738.

meaning_check.note: The name was in ITRANS spelling; now written in IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; naṭeśvarī is naṭa + īśvarī, joined by guṇa.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)
the s of sthā becomes ṣ after the prefix adhi (Pāṇini 8.3.65) and th becomes ṭh next to ṣ (8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya), as a feminine epithet
samasa.vigraha: मिथ्या जगत् मिथ्याजगत्; मिथ्याजगतः अधिष्ठाना मिथ्याजगदधिष्ठाना
samasa.vigraha_iast: mithyā jagat mithyājagat; mithyājagataḥ adhiṣṭhānā mithyājagadadhiṣṭhānā
samasa.explanation: (1) mithyā-jagat 'the unreal world': the indeclinable mithyā 'falsely' qualifies jagat. (2) adhiṣṭhāna 'ground, substratum' is the head, taken in the feminine as an epithet of the Goddess, with the world in the genitive: 'the substratum of the unreal world'.

components.note: adhi + √sthā 'to stand upon'; adhiṣṭhāna with the feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who is the basis of the illusory universe
names.significance: In Advaita the world appears on Brahman as a snake appears on a rope: the appearance is false, the ground is real. She is that ground.
names.previous_split_issues: jagadadhiṣṭhānā was left as one row and jagat given in its sandhi form; it is jagat + adhiṣṭhānā (adhi + sthāna).

samasa.vigraha: मुक्तिम् ददाति इति मुक्तिदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: muktim dadāti iti muktidā
samasa.explanation: -dā 'giving' from √dā is the head and mukti 'liberation' its object, as in name 669.

names.meaning: She who gives liberation
names.significance: Liberation is Her gift; no effort alone wins it without Her grace.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau)
samasa.vigraha: मुक्तिः एव रूपम् मुक्तिरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति मुक्तिरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: muktiḥ eva rūpam muktirūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti muktirūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) mukti 'liberation' is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive -in: 'She whose form is liberation'.

names.meaning: She who is in the form of liberation
names.significance: She does not only give liberation (736); She is liberation itself — the freedom that is the Self's own nature.

samasa.vigraha: लास्यम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा लास्यप्रिया
samasa.vigraha_iast: lāsyam priyam yasyāḥ sā lāsyapriyā
samasa.explanation: priya 'dear' and lāsya 'graceful dance' form a bahuvrīhi with priya placed second: 'She to whom the lāsya dance is dear'.

components.meaning: lāsya, the graceful, gentle dance (the counterpart of Śiva's vigorous tāṇḍava)

names.meaning: She who is fond of the lāsya dance
names.significance: Śiva's tāṇḍava and the Goddess's lāsya together are the dance of the universe: vigor and grace, dissolution and creation.

meaning_check.note: The name was in ITRANS spelling; now written lāsya in IAST.

samasa.vigraha: लयम् करोति इति लयकरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: layam karoti iti layakarī
samasa.explanation: -kara 'making' from √kṛ (feminine -ī) is the head and laya 'dissolution, absorption' its object, as in name 682.

names.meaning: She who causes absorption
names.significance: She brings about the dissolution of the worlds at the end of an age, and in the yogin the absorption of the mind (laya) into its source.

names.meaning: She who exists as modesty in living beings
names.significance: 'To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of modesty' (yā devī sarvabhūteṣu lajjārūpeṇa saṃsthitā) is one of the salutations of the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 5). The seed-syllable hrīṃ is called the lajjā-bīja.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: रम्भा आदिः यासाम् ताः रम्भादयः; रम्भादिभिः वन्दिता रम्भादिवन्दिता
samasa.vigraha_iast: rambhā ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ rambhādayaḥ; rambhādibhiḥ vanditā rambhādivanditā
samasa.explanation: (1) rambhā-ādi 'those of whom Rambhā is the first' (bahuvrīhi): the apsarases. (2) The participle vanditā 'saluted, adored' is the head and takes them in the instrumental of agent.

components.meaning: Rambhā, chief of the apsarases (celestial dancers)
beginning; 'and the others' at the end of a compound

names.meaning: She who is adored by the celestial damsels such as Rambhā
names.significance: The apsarases, famed for their beauty, bow to Her, whose beauty is the source of all beauty.

meaning_check.note: The name was in ITRANS spelling; now written Rambhā in IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: rambhādi was left as one row; it is rambhā + ādi, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.type: saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: भवः एव दावः भवदावः; सुधायाः वृष्टिः सुधावृष्टिः; भवदावे सुधावृष्टिः भवदावसुधावृष्टिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhavaḥ eva dāvaḥ bhavadāvaḥ; sudhāyāḥ vṛṣṭiḥ sudhāvṛṣṭiḥ; bhavadāve sudhāvṛṣṭiḥ bhavadāvasudhāvṛṣṭiḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) bhava-dāva 'the forest fire that is worldly existence': a karmadhāraya of identification (rūpaka). (2) sudhā-vṛṣṭi 'a rain of nectar' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The rain is the head, falling on that fire (locative): 'a rain of nectar on the forest fire of worldly existence'. vṛṣṭi keeps its own feminine i-stem.

names.meaning: She who is the rain of nectar falling on the forest fire of worldly existence
names.significance: Saṃsāra burns like a forest fire; Her grace falls on it like a shower of nectar, quenching it. This begins a run of eight metaphor names (742–749).

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: पापम् एव अरण्यम् पापारण्यम्; दवस्य अनलः दवानलः; पापारण्यस्य दवानला पापारण्यदवानला
samasa.vigraha_iast: pāpam eva araṇyam pāpāraṇyam; davasya analaḥ davānalaḥ; pāpāraṇyasya davānalā pāpāraṇyadavānalā
samasa.explanation: (1) pāpa-araṇya 'the forest that is sin' (rūpaka). (2) dava-anala 'forest fire', literally 'the fire of the forest' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The fire is the head, taken in the feminine as Her epithet, with the forest of sin in the genitive: 'the forest fire to the forest of sins'.

components.note: anala, with the feminine -ā of the epithet

names.meaning: She who is the forest fire that consumes the forest of sins
names.significance: As a wildfire leaves nothing of a forest, Her grace burns away the accumulated sins of the devotee.

meaning_check.note: 'like' weakened the metaphor: a rūpaka identifies, so She is the fire.

names.previous_split_issues: pāpāraṇya and davānalā were each left as one row; they are pāpa + araṇya and dava + anala, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.vigraha: दौर्भाग्यम् एव तूलम् दौर्भाग्यतूलम्; दौर्भाग्यतूलस्य वातूला दौर्भाग्यतूलवातूला
samasa.vigraha_iast: daurbhāgyam eva tūlam daurbhāgyatūlam; daurbhāgyatūlasya vātūlā daurbhāgyatūlavātūlā
samasa.explanation: (1) daurbhāgya-tūla 'the cotton that is misfortune' (rūpaka). (2) vātūlā 'whirlwind, gale' is the head and takes it in the genitive: 'the gale to the cotton of misfortune'.

components.note: abstract noun from durbhaga 'ill-fated' (dus + bhaga), with vṛddhi in both members (Pāṇini 7.3.19 hṛdbhagasindhvante pūrvapade ca)

names.meaning: She who is the gale that drives away the cotton wisps of misfortune
names.significance: Misfortune, however heaped up, is as light as cotton before the wind of Her grace.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: जरा एव ध्वान्तम् जराध्वान्तम्; रवेः प्रभा रविप्रभा; जराध्वान्तस्य रविप्रभा जराध्वान्तरविप्रभा
samasa.vigraha_iast: jarā eva dhvāntam jarādhvāntam; raveḥ prabhā raviprabhā; jarādhvāntasya raviprabhā jarādhvāntaraviprabhā
samasa.explanation: (1) jarā-dhvānta 'the darkness that is old age' (rūpaka). (2) ravi-prabhā 'the light of the sun' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The sunlight is the head and the darkness stands to it in the genitive: 'the sunlight to the darkness of old age'.

names.meaning: She who is the sunlight that dispels the darkness of old age
names.significance: Old age and decay vanish before Her as darkness before the sun; traditionally She grants lasting vigor, and the inner youth of the Self that never ages.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)
jaśtva: p becomes b before the voiced dh (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte), inside the lexicalised compound abdhi 'ocean' ('holder of the waters')

samasa.vigraha: भाग्यम् एव अब्धिः भाग्याब्धिः; भाग्याब्धेः चन्द्रिका भाग्याब्धिचन्द्रिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhāgyam eva abdhiḥ bhāgyābdhiḥ; bhāgyābdheḥ candrikā bhāgyābdhicandrikā
samasa.explanation: (1) bhāgya-abdhi 'the ocean that is good fortune' (rūpaka). (2) candrikā 'moonlight' is the head and takes that ocean in the genitive: 'the moonlight to the ocean of good fortune'.

names.meaning: She who is the moonlight that swells the ocean of good fortune
names.significance: As moonlight raises the tide, Her grace makes the devotee's fortune rise and overflow.

meaning_check.note: candrikā is moonlight, not the full moon; the image is the moon raising the tide.

names.previous_split_issues: bhāgyābdhi was left as one row; it is bhāgya + abdhi, joined by savarṇa-dīrgha.

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa)
samasa.vigraha: भक्तानाम् चित्तानि भक्तचित्तानि; भक्तचित्तानि एव केकिनः भक्तचित्तकेकिनः; भक्तचित्तकेकिनाम् घनाघना भक्तचित्तकेकिघनाघना
samasa.vigraha_iast: bhaktānām cittāni bhaktacittāni; bhaktacittāni eva kekinaḥ bhaktacittakekinaḥ; bhaktacittakekinām ghanāghanā bhaktacittakekighanāghanā
samasa.explanation: (1) bhakta-citta 'the hearts of the devotees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) bhaktacitta-kekin 'the peacocks that are those hearts' (rūpaka; kekin loses its n). (3) ghanāghanā 'dense rain-cloud' is the head and takes the peacocks in the genitive: 'the rain-cloud to the peacocks that are the devotees' hearts'.

components.note: appears as keki- in the compound
an intensive formation from √han, like carācara; feminine -ā

names.meaning: She who is the cloud that gladdens the peacocks who are the hearts of Her devotees
names.significance: Peacocks dance with joy when rain-clouds gather; so the devotee's heart dances at the sight of Her.
names.previous_split_issues: citta was glossed 'consciousness'; here it is the heart or mind. The peacock's stem is kekin.

samasa.vigraha: रोगः एव पर्वतः रोगपर्वतः; रोगपर्वतस्य दम्भोलिः रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः
samasa.vigraha_iast: rogaḥ eva parvataḥ rogaparvataḥ; rogaparvatasya dambholiḥ rogaparvatadambholiḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) roga-parvata 'the mountain that is disease' (rūpaka). (2) dambholi 'thunderbolt' is the head and takes it in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the thunderbolt that shatters the mountain of disease
names.significance: As Indra's thunderbolt struck the mountains, Her grace shatters disease however massive, of body and of mind.

samasa.vigraha: मृत्युः एव दारु मृत्युदारु; मृत्युदारुणः कुठारिका मृत्युदारुकुठारिका
samasa.vigraha_iast: mṛtyuḥ eva dāru mṛtyudāru; mṛtyudāruṇaḥ kuṭhārikā mṛtyudārukuṭhārikā
samasa.explanation: (1) mṛtyu-dāru 'the timber that is death' (rūpaka). (2) kuṭhārikā 'axe' is the head and takes it in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the axe that cuts down the tree of death
names.significance: Death, rooted as a great tree, is felled by Her; She grants immortality, the knowledge of the deathless Self.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: महती ईश्वरी महेश्वरी
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahatī īśvarī maheśvarī
samasa.explanation: mahatī 'great' qualifies īśvarī 'sovereign', the head. The feminine adjective takes its masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva) and mahat becomes mahā- (a morphological replacement); mahā + īśvarī then fuse by guṇa. The name is also the feminine of Maheśvara, 'the consort of the Great Lord'.

components.note: appears as mahā- in the compound

names.meaning: She who is the great Sovereign (Maheśvarī)
names.significance: Maheśvarī is the consort and power of Maheśvara (Śiva), and one of the Mothers; She is the supreme ruler of all.

meaning_check.note: 'supreme goddess' made exact: mahā + īśvarī, the great sovereign.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; maheśvarī is mahā + īśvarī, joined by guṇa.

samasa.vigraha: महती काली महाकाली
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahatī kālī mahākālī
samasa.explanation: mahatī 'great' qualifies kālī; as in name 750 it appears as mahā- (mahat 'great' becomes mahā- before a co-referential member (Pāṇini 6.3.46 ān mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ)). The members meet without sound change.

components.note: appears as mahā- in the compound

components.meaning: Kālī, the dark goddess; she who is time (kāla)

names.meaning: She who is the great Kālī
names.significance: Mahākālī is the fierce form who withdraws all into Herself at the end of time; the Devī Māhātmya invokes Her as the first of its three great forms.

meaning_check.note: The name was in ITRANS spelling; now written Kālī in IAST.

samasa.vigraha: महान् ग्रासः यस्याः सा महाग्रासा
samasa.vigraha_iast: mahān grāsaḥ yasyāḥ sā mahāgrāsā
samasa.explanation: mahat 'great' qualifies grāsa 'mouthful, devouring', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose devouring is great'. mahat appears as mahā- before a co-referential member (Pāṇini 6.3.46).

components.note: appears as mahā- in the compound
grāsa, from √gras 'to swallow', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is the great devourer, swallowing all at the dissolution

components.note: rūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She whose form is Virāj, the cosmic whole
names.significance: In Vedānta Virāj is the Lord as the gross universe taken as one body; all that is seen is Her form.

meaning_check.note: Virāj is now named; the sense is kept.

names.previous_split_issues: virāḍ was given in its sandhi form; the stem is virāj (ḍ only before the voiced r).

samasa.vigraha: विगतम् रजः यस्याः सा विरजा
samasa.vigraha_iast: vigatam rajaḥ yasyāḥ sā virajā
samasa.explanation: vi 'away' stands for vigata 'gone', with rajas 'passion; dust': 'She from whom rajas has gone'. rajas is treated as an a-stem (raja) and takes the feminine -ā.

components.meaning: rajas: the guṇa of passion and activity; dust, impurity
components.note: raja(s), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is without rajas (desire and anger)
names.significance: Desire and anger are born of rajas (Bhagavad Gītā 3.37); She is untouched by them and by all impurity. Virajā is also the name of a sacred river and a goddess of a famous shrine.

sandhi.rule: -as becomes -o before a voiced consonant (Pāṇini 6.1.114 haśi ca)

samasa.vigraha: विश्वतः मुखानि यस्याः सा विश्वतोमुखी
samasa.vigraha_iast: viśvataḥ mukhāni yasyāḥ sā viśvatomukhī
samasa.explanation: The adverb viśvatas 'on all sides' qualifies mukha 'face', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose faces are on every side'. A bahuvrīhi ending in a word for a body part forms its feminine in -ī.

components.note: mukha, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who faces all directions
names.significance: The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (3.3) praises the One whose eyes and faces are everywhere (viśvataś cakṣur uta viśvatomukhaḥ); She sees and is present in every direction.
names.previous_split_issues: viśvato was glossed 'universe'; it is viśvatas 'on all sides', its -as turned to -o.

sandhi.rule: jaśtva: a final k becomes g before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

samasa.vigraha: प्रत्यक् रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रत्यग्रूपा
samasa.vigraha_iast: pratyak rūpam yasyāḥ sā pratyagrūpā
samasa.explanation: pratyak 'turned inward' qualifies rūpa 'form', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is inward', the inner Self. The stem pratyañc 'inward' appears as pratyak at the end of a member.

components.meaning: turned inward, inner; the inner Self
components.note: prati + √añc 'to turn'; pratyak at the end of a member
rūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is the indwelling Self
names.significance: 'A wise one, seeking immortality, turned the eye inward and saw the inner Self (pratyagātman)' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 2.1.1). She is that inner Self, found by turning within.
names.previous_split_issues: pratyag was given in its sandhi form; the word is pratyak (stem pratyañc), g only before the voiced r.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: परम् आकाशम् पराकाशम्; पराकाशम् स्वरूपम् यस्याः सा पराकाशा
samasa.vigraha_iast: param ākāśam parākāśam; parākāśam svarūpam yasyāḥ sā parākāśā
samasa.explanation: (1) para-ākāśa 'the supreme space' (karmadhāraya). (2) As a bahuvrīhi with the feminine -ā: 'She whose own nature is the supreme space'. ākāśa is masculine or neuter, so the -ā shows the name is an epithet; para then appears in its masculine stem.

components.note: ākāśa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is the supreme space (ākāśa)
names.significance: In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (1.9.1) all beings arise from space (ākāśa) and return into it, and the Brahma Sūtra (1.1.22) reads that ākāśa as Brahman. She is that supreme space of consciousness, the material cause of cosmic and individual bodies.

meaning_check.note: The parenthesis on the material cause was moved to the significance.

names.previous_split_issues: The boundary was misplaced: parā + 'kāśā' (glossed 'light/radiance'). The second member is ākāśa 'space', its ā merged with para's a.

samasa.vigraha: प्राणान् ददाति इति प्राणदा
samasa.vigraha_iast: prāṇān dadāti iti prāṇadā
samasa.explanation: -dā 'giving' from √dā is the head and prāṇa 'life-breath' its object.

names.meaning: She who is the giver of life
names.significance: Every breath of every creature is Her gift; She also gives the sensory powers, which the Upaniṣads call prāṇas.

samasa.type: karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau)
samasa.vigraha: प्राणः एव रूपम् प्राणरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति प्राणरूपिणी
samasa.vigraha_iast: prāṇaḥ eva rūpam prāṇarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti prāṇarūpiṇī
samasa.explanation: (1) prāṇa 'life-breath' is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive -in: 'She whose form is prāṇa'.

names.meaning: She whose form is prāṇa, the breath of life
names.significance: After giving life (783) She is life itself; the Brahma Sūtra (1.1.28) shows that the prāṇa praised in the Upaniṣads is Brahman.

meaning_check.note: 'nature of life' made exact: She has prāṇa as Her form.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: मार्ताण्डः च असौ भैरवः च मार्ताण्डभैरवः; मार्ताण्डभैरवेण आराध्या मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: mārtāṇḍaḥ ca asau bhairavaḥ ca mārtāṇḍabhairavaḥ; mārtāṇḍabhairaveṇa ārādhyā mārtāṇḍabhairavārādhyā
samasa.explanation: (1) mārtāṇḍa-bhairava 'Bhairava who is the Sun' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) The gerundive ārādhyā is the head and takes him in the instrumental of agent.

components.meaning: Bhairava, a fierce form of Śiva

names.meaning: She who is worshipped by Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava
names.significance: Traditionally Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava, Śiva in the form of the Sun, dwells with his consort in one of the enclosures of Her city and worships Her there.

meaning_check.note: The name was in ITRANS spelling; now written in IAST.

names.previous_split_issues: bhairavārādhyā was left as one row and glossed 'worshipped by Bhairava'; Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava is one deity, and ārādhyā joins bhairava by savarṇa-dīrgha.
names.uncertain: The place of Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava in Her city follows the usual account; the exact enclosure could not be confirmed against a printed text.

sandhi.rule: yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

samasa.vigraha: राज्यस्य धूः राज्यधूः; मन्त्रिण्याम् न्यस्ता मन्त्रिणीन्यस्ता; मन्त्रिणीन्यस्ता राज्यधूः यया सा मन्त्रिणीन्यस्तराज्यधूः
samasa.vigraha_iast: rājyasya dhūḥ rājyadhūḥ; mantriṇyām nyastā mantriṇīnyastā; mantriṇīnyastā rājyadhūḥ yayā sā mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ
samasa.explanation: (1) rājya-dhur 'the yoke of the kingdom' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mantriṇī-nyasta 'placed on the Mantriṇī' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa with the participle; mantriṇī keeps its ī because this is not a karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with the instrumental yayā: 'She by whom the burden of the kingdom has been placed on the Mantriṇī'. The participle stands first, as is usual in a bahuvrīhi.

components.meaning: the woman minister; Mantriṇī (Śyāmalā), Her chief counselor

components.note: nominative of dhur; the vowel is lengthened before the final r (Pāṇini 8.2.76 rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ)

names.meaning: She who has entrusted the burden of Her kingdom to Her minister, Mantriṇī
names.significance: In the Lalitopākhyāna Mantriṇī (Śyāmalā, Rājaśyāmalā) is Her prime minister and Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī) Her commander; the Empress rules through them. Inwardly, the counsel of the mantra governs the devotee's life.

meaning_check.note: Mantriṇī written in IAST and named as a person, the Goddess's minister.

names.uncertain: Pāṇini 5.4.74 adds the compound-final -a to a compound ending in dhur (…-dhura); the name keeps the bare dhūḥ, a usage also found in epic and Purāṇic Sanskrit. Noted, not a text concern: the verse and the metre support dhūḥ.

sandhi.rule: guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरस्य ईशी त्रिपुरेशी
samasa.vigraha_iast: trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripurasya īśī tripureśī
samasa.explanation: (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' taken as one whole (samāhāra-dvigu). (2) īśī 'sovereign' is the head and takes it in the genitive.

names.meaning: She who is the sovereign of Tripura (the three cities)
names.significance: The three cities are read as every triad — the three bodies, the three states of waking, dream and sleep, the three worlds. In Śrīcakra worship Tripureśī is the presiding goddess of one of the enclosures.

meaning_check.note: Tripura capitalized and glossed.

names.previous_split_issues: No split was given; tripureśī is tri + pura + īśī, joined by guṇa.

samasa.vigraha: जयन्ती सेना यस्याः सा जयत्सेना
samasa.vigraha_iast: jayantī senā yasyāḥ sā jayatsenā
samasa.explanation: The present participle jayat 'conquering' qualifies senā 'army', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose army is conquering'. The feminine jayantī takes its masculine stem jayat inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva); t and s meet with no change.

names.meaning: She whose army is ever victorious
names.significance: Her hosts of śaktis never know defeat; in the Lalitopākhyāna they overthrow Bhaṇḍāsura's armies.

meaning_check.note: 'accustomed only to victory' shortened; the participle says the army is conquering.

names.previous_split_issues: The boundary was misplaced: 'jaya' + 'tsenā'. The participle is jayat 'conquering', and the second member is senā 'army'.

samasa.vigraha: निर्गतम् त्रैगुण्यम् यस्याः सा निस्त्रैगुण्या
samasa.vigraha_iast: nirgatam traiguṇyam yasyāḥ sā nistraiguṇyā
samasa.explanation: nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She from whom the three guṇas have gone'. The s of nis stays s before the voiceless t.

components.note: traiguṇya, abstract noun from triguṇa with vṛddhi, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

names.meaning: She who is beyond the three guṇas
names.significance: 'The Vedas deal with the three guṇas; be free of the three guṇas (nistraiguṇya), Arjuna' (Bhagavad Gītā 2.45). As Prakṛti She is made of the guṇas (763); as pure consciousness She is beyond them.

meaning_check.note: The name was in ITRANS spelling; 'devoid of' became 'beyond'.

sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

samasa.vigraha: परा च असौ अपरा च परापरा
samasa.vigraha_iast: parā ca asau aparā ca parāparā
samasa.explanation: parā 'supreme' and aparā 'not supreme' both describe the one Goddess: 'She who is both the higher and the lower'. Inside the compound parā takes its masculine stem para (puṃvadbhāva), which fuses with aparā by savarṇa-dīrgha.

names.meaning: She who is both the supreme (parā) and the non-supreme (aparā)
names.significance: The Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (1.1.4) speaks of two knowledges, the higher (parā) and the lower (aparā); She is both, the transcendent and the manifest. In the Tantras Parāparā is also the middle of three levels (parā, parāparā, aparā).

meaning_check.note: Rendered the two terms; the earlier gloss left them untranslated.

names.uncertain: Read as 'both supreme and non-supreme' (karmadhāraya) or as 'the intermediate, Parāparā' (the middle of the Tantric triad).

external_sandhi.rule: savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the double avagraha (ऽऽ) marks the long ā of ānanda absorbed in the fusion

verse_notes.note: Read citkalā | ānandakalikā (728–729): the double avagraha shows where the second name begins.
Names 738–740 alliterate on l (lāsyapriyā, layakarī, lajjā).
Names 742–749 are a run of eight metaphors (rūpaka): each names an evil as fire, forest, cotton, darkness, ocean, mountain or timber, and Her as what quenches, burns, scatters, dispels or cuts it.

external_sandhi.rule: visarga becomes r before a vowel or voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

verse_notes.note: The r of -dambholir- is the visarga of rogaparvatadambholiḥ (748); name 749 begins mṛtyu-.
Names 750–753 all begin with mahā-; 753 is mahā + aśanā 'whose eating is great', not mahā + śanā. Names 751 and 755–756 recall the Devī Māhātmya.
tryambakā (762) is tri + ambaka 'three-eyed', not tri + ambā.
durārādhyā (771) answers sukhārādhyā (681): easy to worship for the devoted, hard for the undisciplined.
Spelling traps: virāḍrūpā has ḍ for the j of virāj, pratyagrūpā g for the k of pratyak; parākāśā is para + ākāśa 'space', not parā + kāśā.
jayatsenā (788) is jayat + senā, not jaya + tsenā; mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ (786) ends in dhūḥ, the nominative of dhur 'burden'.

report.summary: Checked all 63 names of ślokas 141–150 against text.json: sandhi at every member and prefix junction (including the external fusion citkalā + ānandakalikā), layered samāsa analyses with pausa-form vigrahas, and each meaning against its analysis. Three word boundaries were wrong in the old splits and are corrected (753 mahā + aśanā, not śanā; 782 para + ākāśa, not parā + kāśā; 788 jayat + senā, not jaya + tsenā). Meanings were replaced for 728 (kalā not rendered), 756 ('and other asuras' is not in the name) and 772 (ādharṣa is 'assailing', not 'control'). No problem was found in the Sanskrit text.
